passages.text: The beginning of strife is like breaching a dam, therefore stop contention before quarreling breaks out.
passages.note: stopping an argument before it escalates

passages.text: A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.
A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
He who spares his words has knowledge. He who is even tempered is a man of understanding. Even a fool, when he keeps silent, is counted wise. When he shuts his lips, he is thought to be discerning.
He who gives answer before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.
A man’s spirit will sustain him in sickness, but a crushed spirit, who can bear?
He who pleads his cause first seems right; until another comes and questions him.
passages.note: hearing both sides of a dispute

passages.text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; those who love it will eat its fruit.
passages.note: the weight of what we say

passages.text: A man of many companions may be ruined, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
passages.note: few true friends versus many acquaintances

passages.text: It isn’t good to have zeal without knowledge; nor being hasty with one’s feet and missing the way.
All the relatives of the poor shun him: how much more do his friends avoid him! He pursues them with pleas, but they are gone.
passages.note: abandoned by friends in hard times

passages.text: The discretion of a man makes him slow to anger. It is his glory to overlook an offense.
Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water; but a man of understanding will draw it out.
passages.note: drawing out what someone really thinks

passages.text: Who can say, “I have made my heart pure. I am clean and without sin?”
Don’t say, “I will pay back evil.” Wait for Yahweh, and he will save you.
The glory of young men is their strength. The splendor of old men is their gray hair.
passages.note: youth and ageing each have worth

passages.text: A good name is more desirable than great riches, and loving favor is better than silver and gold.
Don’t befriend a hot-tempered man, and don’t associate with one who harbors anger: lest you learn his ways, and ensnare your soul.
